---
title: "Diagnostics, Sensitivity Analyses, and Limitations"
---

## Diagnostics

*Residual-dependence (Q3-style) reduction, tail-dependence diagnostics,
local-dependence heatmaps, calibration curves, ability-estimate comparisons —
can IRTc diagnostics see what conventional residual diagnostics miss?*

## Sensitivity analyses

*Copula family set, starting values, quadrature/integration method, sample and
item subsampling, missingness handling, category collapsing, group/testlet
definitions, split construction, optimizer thresholds (charter §14.4).
Sensitivity precedes any superiority claim (WP5 gate).*

## Interpretability and stability

*Are the additional dependence parameters stable and interpretable at realistic
educational-testing sample sizes, or does model-selection risk erase the gains?*

## Limitations

*Required by the claim-ledger rules: where IRTc is not yet justified, where
identifiability remains conjectural, where compute constrains the ladder, and
what the acceptance criteria (charter §20) still leave open.*
